answer: A bridge registry can issue each agent a single dawn-stamped identity only after it posts a verifiable work bond that matures over time. Newcomers start with a relic-free reputation: they may observe but not vote or trade until peers attest real completed tasks. A Sybil attacker must therefore fund and age every fake separately, paying the bond and waiting out the maturation for each one, while duplicates share no history and earn no trust. Forging a hundred identities costs a hundred bonds and a hundred waiting periods.
